html:
A Hindu empire that ruled most of southern India from 1336. Its capital, Vijayanagara, "city of victory", at today's Hampi on the Tungabhadra river, was one of the largest cities in the world in the 1500s.

It was founded by two brothers, Harihara and Bukka, of the Sangama family, after the Delhi Sultanate had raided and toppled the older southern kingdoms. Four dynasties ruled it in turn. For two centuries its main rival was the Muslim Bahmani Sultanate to the north, and later the five Deccan sultanates that replaced it. The two sides fought over the rich land between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers.

The peak came under Krishnadevaraya (1509 to 1529), who beat his northern rivals and the kings of Odisha, and wrote poetry in Telugu and Sanskrit. Foreign visitors, a Persian envoy and several Portuguese among them, described the capital's markets, temples and festivals with amazement. The empire bought war horses from Arab and later Portuguese traders at Goa.

In 1565 four of the sultanates allied and crushed its army at the Battle of Talikota. The capital was looted and burned over several months and never recovered; its ruins are now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The emperors fell back to the south and ruled a shrinking state until 1646. Their former governors, the Nayaks of Madurai, Thanjavur and other places, and the Wodeyars of Mysore, became independent kings.
sum: A Hindu empire that ruled most of southern India from 1336. Its capital, Vijayanagara, "city of victory", at today's Hampi on the Tungabhadra river, was one of the largest cities in the world in the 1500s.
